classification.difficultyReason: Each triangle requires an angle-sum equation and inverse operations; two parts require recognising a marked right angle.

content.prompt: Use the angle sum of a triangle to find the value of the pronumeral. Show full working out.

spec.description: Triangle with the base rising slightly to the right; a at the upper vertex, 70 degrees at lower left and 30 degrees at lower right.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens and unknown label appear; the supplied answer is separate.

spec.description: Downward-pointing triangle with a at upper left, 116 degrees at upper right and 24 degrees near the bottom vertex.
Right triangle with horizontal base, vertical right side and a right-angle square at lower right; 32 degrees at lower left and a at upper right.
spec.answerVisibility: The 90-degree value is represented by the source square, not an added numerical label.

answer.worked:
The marked right angle is $90^\circ$. Angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}a+32+90&=180\\a+122&=180\\a&=58^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Rotated right triangle with a at upper left, a right-angle square at the right-hand vertex and 71 degrees at the bottom vertex.
spec.mathematics: The marked sides at the right-hand vertex are perpendicular; a+90+71=180.

answer.worked:
The marked right angle is $90^\circ$. Angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}a+90+71&=180\\a+161&=180\\a&=19^\circ\end{align*}$$
